Thousands flee as First Nations bear the brunt of Canada's wildfires
===========================================================

Thousands flee from fires burning out of control, leaving behind scorched landscapes and shattered communities. More than 2,182 First Nations people have been forced to evacuate their homes, with Thirteen Nations currently under evacuation orders. The situation is dire, with residents having mere minutes to gather their belongings before flames overtake their homes.

## Devastating impact on First Nations communities

The Namaygoosisagagun (Collins) First Nation watched as one blaze ravaged its entire community in less than an hour, forcing residents to flee by boat. "It is with heartfelt sadness that I share that our member First Nation, Namaygoosisagagun First Nation, has been devastated by an unexpected and fast-moving wildfire that advanced toward and through the community, causing extensive damage and destruction to homes and community buildings," said Anishinabek Nation Grand Council Chief Linda Debassige in a statement. In addition to Namaygoosisagagun, Whitesand First Nation, Kiashke Zaaging Anishinaabek, and Animbiigoo Zaagi’igan Anishinaabek are among those impacted by evacuation orders. [claim:thousands-flee-as-first-nations-bear-the-brunt-of-canada-s-wildfires:1,5,9](https://grist.org/indigenous/thousands-flee-as-first-nations-bear-the-brunt-of-canadas-wildfires/)

The wildfires have been particularly devastating in Ontario, where seven First Nations have fled the 193 fires now burning there. Dozens of non-Indigenous communities throughout the province have also been ordered to evacuate. The effect of these evacuation orders is greatest in areas where resources and support are already scarce. [claim:thousands-flee-as-first-nations-bear-the-brunt-of-canada-s-wildfires:2,7,10](https://grist.org/indigenous/thousands-flee-as-first-nations-bear-the-brunt-of-canadas-wildfires/)

In contrast, non-Indigenous communities within close proximity to these First Nations have access to better resources and support, including evacuation assistance and recovery funding. Meaghan Daniel, a lawyer representing the Collins First Nation, stated that community members went door-to-door warning their neighbors, and more than two dozen people fled by boat just as the flames approached. "To be clear, if Namaygoosisagagun is denied access to the emergency and rebuilding supports available to recognized First Nations, it will not simply suffer a slower recovery," she wrote in a letter to Indigenous Services Minister Mandy Gull-Masty. "It may lose forever the opportunity to rebuild the community its members spent decades creating." [claim:thousands-flee-as-first-nations-bear-the-brunt-of-canada-s-wildfires:13,17](https://grist.org/indigenous/thousands-flee-as-first-nations-bear-the-brunt-of-canadas-wildfires/) [claim:thousands-flee-as-first-nations-bear-the-brunt-of-canada-s-wildfires:18](https://grist.org/indigenous/thousands-flee-as-first-nations-bear-the-brunt-of-canadas-wildfires/)

The uncertainty and danger surrounding these wildfires have left the fate of affected communities hanging in the balance. The Namaygoosisagagun First Nation's struggle for recognition has long been an issue, and the government's response to its current situation raises significant concerns. [claim:thousands-flee-as-first-nations-bear-the-brunt-of-canada-s-wildfires:15,16,19](https://grist.org/indigenous/thousands-flee-as-first-nations-bear-the-brunt-of-canadas-wildfires/)

The lack of recognition for the Namaygoosisagagun First Nation has significant consequences, including the denial of access to emergency and rebuilding supports. As Meaghan Daniel so eloquently put it, "The question is not merely whether recovery will be delayed." The question is whether the community will be able to rebuild and recover in the face of adversity. [claim:thousands-flee-as-first-nations-bear-the-brunt-of-canada-s-wildfires:20](https://grist.org/indigenous/thousands-flee-as-first-nations-bear-the-brunt-of-canadas-wildfires/)
